title: Consumption
coreMove: Decode purchases as signals of traits, not only as satisfaction of needs or wealth display.
sourcePressure: The source widens conspicuous consumption into consumer signaling, where purchases communicate wealth, conscientiousness, adventurousness, and identity.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The writer makes the chapter only about luxury status and misses conscientiousness, adventurousness, and identity signals.

sourceAnchors.name: conspicuous consumption as one pattern among several
sourceAnchors.detail: The source says conspicuous consumption is only one signaling pattern in a broader landscape.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The expensive object is one dialect, not the whole language.

sourceAnchors.name: purchases signaling conscientiousness
sourceAnchors.detail: The source says purchases can signal conscientiousness.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The tidy purchase can say I plan, maintain, and notice small duties.

sourceAnchors.name: purchases signaling adventurousness and identity
sourceAnchors.detail: The source says purchases can signal adventurousness and identity.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: A purchase can announce the kind of risk, tribe, or self a person wants others to read.

exampleSpecs.domain: bikepacking gear checkout before a weekend trip
exampleSpecs.audience: a friend reading a purchase beyond price
exampleSpecs.stakes: a rider may be signaling competence and adventurousness more than comfort
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Megan watches Olivier lay out the repair kit before the carbon frame and realizes the signal is not wealth but field readiness.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Chain oil darkens the rag beside an unopened titanium stove.

exampleSpecs.audience: a parent noticing conscientiousness signals without turning them into moral rank
exampleSpecs.stakes: care can become display through objects children carry
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You see Anya's labeled containers and separate actual allergy care from the visible signal of being the organized parent.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You notice the tiny printed labels before the sandwich.

exampleSpecs.audience: a manager interpreting a contractor's background objects
exampleSpecs.stakes: identity signals may substitute for proof of reliability
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: What does the analog notebook say that the task history does not?
exampleSpecs.firstImage: What does the analog notebook announce before Chris answers?

exampleSpecs.audience: a vendor reading customer identity signals around sustainability
exampleSpecs.stakes: the tote may communicate identity more than carrying capacity
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: "No bag, thanks," Yusuf says, and Marit notices he holds the old co-op tote label outward while declining one more bag.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "No bag, thanks," Yusuf says with the faded co-op logo facing the line.

exampleSpecs.audience: a junior associate choosing what competence to signal
exampleSpecs.stakes: a too-expensive suit may signal wealth while weakening conscientious fit
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The associate chooses the repaired navy jacket because the visible tailoring signals care without making the dinner about money.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Rain beads on the coat-check tags beside a row of black garment bags.

exampleSpecs.audience: a trip leader reading overpacked gear kindly
exampleSpecs.stakes: novices signal eagerness and identity while creating safety burdens
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: It took Megan one overloaded ridge walk to teach packing as signal management: carry what proves readiness, leave what only performs belonging.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: It took Megan one overloaded ridge walk to weigh every dangling carabiner differently.

skillTargets: distinguish trait signaling from need satisfaction
evaluate when a purchase signal helps or distorts judgment

tryThisNowSpec: Look at one object you chose to make visible today. Name the trait it signals: wealth, care, taste, adventurousness, identity, or discipline.
